matched.note: Same defect: cmd/bootstrap/run.sh:23 `results="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/smine-bootstrap-results.jsonl"` is a fixed, non-run-scoped path appended to across stages with no truncation/uniqueness. Golden frames it as a multi-user race risk; SP-003 frames it as unbounded growth/run ambiguity — same root cause (fixed shared path, no per-run scoping), different consequence emphasis.

Identical defect: Registry struct's new loadedModTime/loadedSize fields inserted non-alphabetically into the unexported field group (mu, loadedModTime, loadedSize, repos), violating RULE-GOLANG-STRUCT-002.

uncataloged.reason: Confirmed against code: cmd/hooks/acdsl-policy-guard.sh:43 unconditionally denies Write/Edit to acdsl/registry.local.json whenever mode is gated or strict. But internal/acdsl/policy.go's policySurface (the Go-side frozen self-management surface, lines ~31-35) does NOT include registry.local.json — it is instead governed by overlayViolations (policy.go:139-170), which reads registry.local.json and permits entries listed in policy.local_overrides. acdsl/README.md:32-35 confirms the overlay is meant to be policy-gated (sanctioned entries accepted), not flatly denied. So the hook's blanket deny blocks the sanctioned local-override path via normal tool calls even though the authoritative acdsl check would allow it. This is a distinct root cause from the golden's cataloged acdsl-policy-guard.sh findings (GV3-045 missing test, GV3-068 path-canonicalization bypass, GV3-125 case-sensitivity bypass, GV3-199 Bash-command blind spot) — none of which describe the local_overrides/hook conflict. Not a known false positive. Genuine in-range defect the golden does not catalog.

Confirmed against skills/smine/smine-apply/SKILL.md:31 — the casual lockout ('Casual lockout (hard gate)') is stated purely as prose the implementing agent must follow (read frontmatter, check origin: user, skip if absent); there is no script or deterministic diff check anywhere in the pipeline (smine-apply, smine-skills:45, smine-orchestrate:41) enforcing it — smine-orchestrate's Judge-stage check is likewise agent-executed prose ('a violation is a hard invariant breach — revert the commit'), not a mechanical/code-level gate. This is a different root cause from GV5-237 (which is about a specific loophole — new-skill proposals being exempted via auto-stamped origin: user — that exists even when the lockout is followed correctly), and from GV3-013 (permissions-route allow/deny gap). No golden entry catalogs the general 'no mechanical backstop, agent-compliance-only' architecture claim. Not a known false positive. Genuine in-range defect the golden does not catalog.

Confirmed against code: routines/smine-nightly/run.sh's newly-added Stage-3 reconcile block (git diff shows this whole `if [[ -f "$repo_root/repos.json" && -s "$settings_file" ]]; then ... fi` block, including the jq/mv line, is new in this range) does `jq ... "$settings_file" > "$settings_file.tmp" && mv "$settings_file.tmp" "$settings_file"` — the `>` redirection creates/truncates $settings_file.tmp before jq's exit status is known, and if jq fails the `&&` short-circuits before the mv, leaving the stray/partial .tmp file behind in ~/.claude/. This is a distinct root cause from the golden's cataloged findings on this same block (GV3-099 and GV3-114, both about missing test coverage of the reconcile guard/postconditions, and GV3-196, about the merge target lacking a path denylist) — none of which describe the leftover-tmp-file-on-jq-failure defect. Not a known false positive. Genuine in-range defect the golden does not catalog.

Confirmed against code: internal/acdsl/policy.go:258-259, `workRules, _ := ParseRules(workLines)` and `baseRules, _ := ParseRules(baseLines)` inside ruleDelta, discard ParseRules' error return on both sides. An unparseable declaration file therefore silently yields incomplete/empty rule sets rather than surfacing a parse failure, skewing the added/removed/changed classification. This is a distinct function and root cause from the golden's cataloged parse-error findings on this file (GV3-097, about basePolicy's own unparseable-base-policy hard-error branch being untested; GV3-048/GV3-108/GV3-112, about other unexercised branches in policyBase/effectiveAllowlist) — none address ruleDelta's own ParseRules error discard. Not a known false positive. Genuine in-range defect the golden does not catalog.
